lessons.title: Short-Day, Intermediate, and Long-Day Varieties
lessons.body: Onion varieties are grouped by how many hours of daylight they need to form bulbs. This is called photoperiod. In Africa, most countries lie between the equator and 35Â°S or 35Â°N, so day length is fairly consistent year-round. Short-day varieties need 10â12 hours of daylight to bulb. They are best for regions like Senegal, Mali, Sudan, and northern Nigeria where days are shorter. Intermediate varieties need 12â14 hours and suit places like Kenya, Tanzania, and Zambia. Long-day varieties need 14â16 hours and are only for far southern Africa like South Africa's Western Cape in summer. If you plant a long-day variety in a short-day region, it will grow leaves but never form a bulb. If you plant a short-day variety in a long-day region, it may bulb too early and stay small. So always match variety to your latitude. Ask your local agricultural extension officer for the day length in your area. A simple rule: if you are within 10 degrees of the equator, choose short-day types. Between 10 and 20 degrees, choose intermediate. Beyond 20 degrees, you can try long-day in summer. Examples: 'Red Creole' is short-day, 'Texas Grano 502' is intermediate, 'Yellow Globe' is long-day. Plant at the right time too: short-day onions should be planted in cool months so they bulb before hot weather. In Kenya, plant short-day varieties in AprilâMay. In Nigeria, plant in OctoberâNovember. Always check with local farmers what works.

lessons.title: Hybrid vs. Open-Pollinated Varieties
lessons.body: Hybrid onion seeds are produced by crossing two parent lines. They give uniform plants, higher yields, and better disease resistance, but you cannot save seed from themâthe next generation will be mixed and poor. Hybrid seeds cost more: a 100g packet may cost $15â$30, while open-pollinated (OP) seeds cost $5â$10. Open-pollinated varieties are stable, so you can save seeds from your best bulbs and replant. They are cheaper and good for local markets, but yields may be 20â30% lower than hybrids. For African smallholders, OP varieties like 'Red Creole' and 'Bombay Red' are popular because they are hardy and seed can be saved. Hybrids like 'Sivan' or 'Candy' give bigger bulbs but require good management: fertilizer, water, and pest control. If you are a beginner, start with OP varieties. If you sell to supermarkets or export, hybrids give the uniform size and color buyers want. To save OP seed, select the best 10â20 bulbs at harvest, store them until the next season, then replant them in isolation from other onion varieties. Let them flower and produce seed. Collect seed when the heads dry and turn brown. Store in a cool, dry place. Never save seed from hybridsâyou will waste time and money. Also, buy certified seed from reputable suppliers to avoid mixing. In many African countries, local seed companies like Seed Co, East-West Seed, and Kenya Seed Company sell both types. Check the label for 'F1 hybrid' or 'OP'.

lessons.title: Disease-Resistant and Storage Varieties
lessons.body: Onions suffer from diseases like purple blotch, downy mildew, and neck rot. Choosing resistant varieties reduces losses without chemicals. For purple blotch, look for 'Red Creole' and 'Texas Grano 502' which have some tolerance. For downy mildew, 'Candy' and 'Sivan' are resistant. In East Africa, 'Bombay Red' resists thrips and purple blotch. In West Africa, 'Violet de Galmi' is popular for its resistance to downy mildew. Storage ability is also key. Onions that store well have thick, dry skins and high dry matter. 'Red Creole' stores 3â4 months. 'Yellow Globe' stores 5â6 months. 'Copra' and 'Hytech' are hybrids that store 6â8 months. To store onions, cure them first: spread bulbs in a dry, shaded area for 10â14 days until necks are tight and skins rustle. Then store in a cool, dark, well-ventilated place. Ideal temperature is 0â5Â°C, but in Africa, use a ventilated shed or raised platform. Avoid piling onions more than 30 cm deep. Check weekly and remove rotten bulbs. If you plan to sell over several months, choose long-storage varieties. If you sell immediately after harvest, disease resistance matters more. Always buy seed labeled with resistance info. Ask your extension officer for the latest resistant varieties in your area. Some varieties like 'Red Creole' are dual-purpose: resistant and store well. But no variety is immune to all diseases, so rotate crops with maize or beans for at least 2 years.

lessons.title: Choosing Varieties for Your Climate
lessons.body: Your climate determines which onion variety will thrive. Onions grow best in mild temperatures (15â25Â°C) with plenty of sun. In hot, dry areas like northern Nigeria or Senegal, choose short-day varieties that mature fast, such as 'Red Creole' or 'Bombay Red'. They bulb in 90â110 days. In cooler highlands like Kenya's Rift Valley or Ethiopia, intermediate varieties like 'Texas Grano 502' work well, maturing in 110â130 days. In Mediterranean climates like South Africa's Western Cape, long-day varieties like 'Yellow Globe' are best. Rainfall matters too. Onions hate waterlogged soil. If your area gets heavy rain, plant on raised beds 20â30 cm high. In dry areas, you need irrigation. Choose varieties that tolerate heat: 'Red Creole' and 'Violet de Galmi' are good. For cold areas, 'Yellow Globe' and 'Copra' tolerate frost. Also consider your soil. Onions prefer sandy loam with pH 6.0â6.8. If your soil is heavy clay, add compost and plant on ridges. Test your soil with a simple kit from an agro-dealer. Altitude matters: above 1500 m, choose intermediate or long-day types. Below 1000 m, choose short-day. Talk to nearby farmers about what works. Visit a local market and see which onions sell bestâred, white, or yellow. Then choose a variety that matches both your climate and market demand. Always plant a small trial plot of a new variety before planting your whole field.

lessons.title: Seed Quality and Germination Testing
lessons.body: Good seed is the foundation of a good onion crop. Always buy certified seed from a reputable agro-dealer. Check the label for: variety name, lot number, germination percentage, and expiry date. Onion seed loses viability quicklyâgermination drops by 10% every year if stored poorly. Never use seed older than 2 years. To test germination at home, do this: count 100 seeds. Soak a clean cloth in water and wring it out. Place seeds evenly on the cloth, fold it, and put it in a plastic bag. Keep it in a warm place (20â25Â°C) for 10â14 days. Keep the cloth moist but not dripping. After 14 days, count how many seeds have sprouted. If 85 or more sprouted, the seed is good. If 70â84, use more seed per plot (increase seeding rate by 20%). If below 70, buy new seed. You can also do a float test: put seeds in a glass of water. Viable seeds sink; dead seeds float. But this is less reliable. Store your seed in an airtight container with a desiccant like silica gel or dry rice. Keep it in a cool, dark place. Never store seed in a plastic bag in the sun. For planting, use 4â5 kg of seed per hectare if germination is above 85%. If germination is lower, increase to 6â7 kg. Always sow fresh seed each season for best results.

lessons.title: Understanding Seed Catalogs and Suppliers
lessons.body: Seed catalogs list varieties with details like maturity days, disease resistance, and storage life. But many catalogs are written for large farms in Europe or America. As an African smallholder, you need to read between the lines. Look for varieties that match your day length and climate. Ignore terms like 'long-day' if you are near the equator. Check the 'days to maturity'âthis is from transplanting, not sowing. In Africa, add 10â14 days for nursery time. Also check 'bolting resistance'âonions that bolt (flower early) produce small bulbs. Choose varieties with good bolting resistance for your planting season. When buying from local suppliers, ask for the latest seed lot and check the germination percentage on the label. Reputable suppliers in Africa include: East-West Seed (East Africa), Seed Co (Southern Africa), Kenya Seed Company, and Technisem (West Africa). You can also order from online suppliers like Seedman or Baker Creek, but check if they ship to your country and if the variety suits your climate. Always buy from a supplier who stores seed properlyânot in a hot warehouse. If you buy from a market vendor, ask to see the original packet. Avoid seed sold in unlabeled bottles or bags. Join a farmer group and buy in bulk to get discounts. Also, ask your extension officer for a list of recommended varieties for your region. Keep records of what you plant and how it performs, so you know what to buy next season.

quiz.q: What determines whether an onion variety is short-day, intermediate, or long-day?
options: B) The number of daylight hours needed to form bulbs
quiz.explanation: Photoperiod, or day length, triggers bulb formation in onions.

quiz.q: Which type of onion variety is best for a region near the equator?
quiz.explanation: Near the equator, day length is around 12 hours, so short-day varieties bulb properly.

quiz.q: What happens if you plant a long-day onion variety in a short-day region?
options: C) It grows leaves but no bulb
D) It grows very large bulbs
quiz.explanation: Long-day varieties need more daylight hours to trigger bulbing, so they remain vegetative in short-day conditions.

quiz.q: Which of these is a short-day onion variety?
quiz.explanation: Red Creole is a well-known short-day variety suited to low latitudes.

quiz.q: In Kenya, when should short-day onions be planted?
quiz.explanation: In Kenya, planting in AprilâMay allows bulbs to form before hot weather.

quiz.q: What is a key disadvantage of hybrid onion varieties?
options: C) You cannot save seed from them
D) They are more susceptible to diseases
quiz.explanation: Hybrid seeds are F1 crosses, so saved seed will not produce the same variety.

quiz.q: Which type of onion seed is cheaper and allows seed saving?
quiz.explanation: Open-pollinated varieties are stable and can be saved for replanting.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost difference between hybrid and open-pollinated onion seeds?
options: B) Hybrids cost about the same
quiz.explanation: Hybrid seeds are more expensive due to controlled cross-pollination.

quiz.q: How can you save seed from open-pollinated onions?
options: A) Collect seeds from flowers after bolting
B) Cut the bulbs and dry them
C) Use the small bulbs from the harvest
D) Store bulbs and replant them next season
quiz.explanation: Select best bulbs, store, replant, and let them flower to produce seed.

quiz.q: What does 'F1 hybrid' on a seed label mean?
quiz.explanation: F1 indicates the first filial generation from a cross of two parent lines.

quiz.q: Which disease-resistant onion variety is known for tolerance to purple blotch?
quiz.explanation: Red Creole has some tolerance to purple blotch.

quiz.q: What is a key characteristic of onion varieties that store well?
quiz.explanation: Thick, dry skins help prevent moisture loss and rot during storage.

quiz.q: How long can 'Yellow Globe' onions typically be stored?
quiz.explanation: Yellow Globe is a good storage variety, lasting 5â6 months under proper conditions.

quiz.q: What is the first step before storing onions?
options: B) Cure them in a dry, shaded area
D) Cut off the tops immediately
quiz.explanation: Curing for 10â14 days dries the neck and skins, improving storage life.

quiz.q: Which variety is known for resistance to downy mildew in West Africa?
quiz.explanation: Violet de Galmi is popular in West Africa for its downy mildew resistance.

quiz.q: What is the ideal temperature range for storing onions?
quiz.explanation: Cool temperatures slow down spoilage and sprouting.

quiz.q: In hot, dry areas of Africa, which onion variety is recommended?
quiz.explanation: Red Creole is a short-day variety that tolerates heat and matures fast.

quiz.q: What is the preferred soil pH for onions?
quiz.explanation: Onions grow best in slightly acidic to neutral soil, pH 6.0â6.8.

quiz.q: Why should you plant onions on raised beds in heavy rainfall areas?
quiz.explanation: Raised beds prevent waterlogging, which onions cannot tolerate.

quiz.q: What should you do before planting a new onion variety on a large scale?
options: B) Test it in a small trial plot
quiz.explanation: A small trial helps you assess performance and suitability for your farm.

quiz.q: How often does onion seed germination typically drop if stored poorly?
quiz.explanation: Poor storage can reduce germination by about 10% each year.

quiz.q: What is the correct way to do a simple germination test for onion seed?
options: A) Soak seeds in water and count floaters
B) Place seeds on moist cloth in a warm place for 10â14 days
C) Plant seeds in soil and wait 30 days
D) Put seeds in a plastic bag in the sun
quiz.explanation: The cloth method is standard for testing germination percentage.

quiz.q: If 80 out of 100 onion seeds germinate, what should you do?
quiz.explanation: 80% germination is acceptable but requires a higher seeding rate to achieve desired plant population.

quiz.q: How should you store onion seed for long-term viability?
options: A) In a plastic bag in the sun
B) In an airtight container with desiccant in a cool, dark place
C) In the refrigerator in an open bowl
D) In a paper bag on a shelf
quiz.explanation: Airtight containers with desiccant prevent moisture damage and maintain germination.

quiz.q: What is the recommended seeding rate for onions per hectare if germination is above 85%?
quiz.explanation: 4â5 kg per hectare is standard for good quality seed.

quiz.q: When reading a seed catalog, what does 'days to maturity' usually refer to?
options: D) From flowering to seed set
quiz.explanation: Days to maturity typically counts from transplanting, not sowing.

quiz.q: Why is 'bolting resistance' important when choosing an onion variety?
options: B) Bolting reduces bulb size and quality
quiz.explanation: Bolting (flowering) diverts energy from bulb formation, resulting in smaller bulbs.

quiz.q: Which of these is a reputable seed supplier in East Africa?
quiz.explanation: All three are well-known seed companies operating in Africa.

quiz.q: What should you check on a seed packet label before buying?
options: A) Variety name and lot number
quiz.explanation: All these details ensure you are buying quality seed.

quiz.q: Why is it risky to buy onion seed from unlabeled bottles at a market?
options: A) It may be old or low quality
B) It may be a different variety
C) It may have low germination
quiz.explanation: Unlabeled seed lacks quality assurance and may be misrepresented.
